examples.en: A patrol car is parked in front of the police substation.
A patrol car goes around our neighborhood every night.

examples.ko: 순찰차를 보면 운전을 더 조심하게 돼요.
examples.en: When I see a patrol car, I drive more carefully.

examples.ko: 순찰차 한 대가 사이렌을 켜고 지나갔어요.
examples.en: A patrol car passed by with its siren on.
The police officer got out of the patrol car and asked me for directions.

examples.ko: 아파트 입구에 순찰차가 있어서 마음이 놓여요.
examples.en: There is a patrol car at the apartment entrance, so I feel safe.

explain: 일상에서는 '경찰차'라고도 많이 말해요. 순찰차는 동네를 돌며 살피는 차라는 느낌이 있어서 '순찰차가 돌다', '순찰차를 보다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people also say '경찰차' (police car). 순찰차 carries the feel of a car that goes around an area keeping watch, so phrases like '순찰차가 돌다' (a patrol car makes its rounds) are common.

examples.en: The baby is still clumsy at using a spoon.

examples.ko: 숟가락질을 배우는 중이라 밥을 많이 흘려요.
examples.en: He is learning to use a spoon, so he spills a lot of rice.
Grandfather's hands shake, so using a spoon is hard for him.
Don't just keep spooning rice; eat some side dishes too.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 이제 혼자 숟가락질을 해요.
examples.en: My child now uses a spoon by himself.
Using a spoon is easier than using chopsticks.

explain: '-질'이 붙어서 손으로 반복해서 하는 동작을 가리켜요. '젓가락질'과 짝으로 자주 나와서 아이가 밥 먹는 법을 배울 때 많이 말해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-질' marks a repeated hand action. It often pairs with '젓가락질' (using chopsticks) and comes up a lot when children learn to eat.

examples.en: I heard a thief sneaked into the empty house.
The cat sneaks under the car.

examples.ko: 아이가 무서워서 이불 속으로 숨어들고 말았어요.
examples.en: The child was scared and ended up hiding away under the blanket.
You must not sneak into a theater.
There was nowhere to slip away to, so I kept walking.
He quietly sneaked into the building.

explain: '숨다'는 그냥 몸을 감춘다는 느낌이고, '숨어들다'는 어딘가 안으로 들어가서 숨는 느낌이 있어요. '-(으)로 숨어들다'처럼 장소와 함께 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '숨어드는, 숨어든'이 돼요.
explain_en: '숨다' simply means to hide, while '숨어들다' feels like going into somewhere and hiding there, so it is used with a place, as in '-(으)로 숨어들다'. The ㄹ drops before some endings: 숨어드는, 숨어든.

examples.en: I went up the stairs and now I'm out of breath.
I'm so out of breath that I can't talk.
The mountain was high, so I got more breathless as I climbed.
You must have run here out of breath; your face is red.
If you're out of breath, you can rest for a moment.

examples.ko: 많이 숨차 보이는데 물 좀 마셔요.
examples.en: You look very out of breath, so have some water.

explain: '숨이 차다'라고 띄어서도 많이 말해요. 달리기, 계단, 등산처럼 몸을 쓴 뒤에 숨이 가쁠 때 써요.
explain_en: People also say '숨이 차다' as separate words. It is used when you are short of breath after physical effort such as running, stairs or hiking.

examples.en: Meat grilled over a charcoal fire tastes different.
Sweet potatoes are cooking over the charcoal fire.
At the campsite, we started by lighting the charcoal.
Grill quickly before the charcoal goes out.
This restaurant is famous for its charcoal-grilled ribs.

examples.ko: 밀폐된 공간에서 숯불을 피우면 질식 위험이 있어요.
examples.en: Lighting charcoal in a closed space carries a risk of suffocation.

explain: '숯불에 굽다', '숯불을 피우다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 식당에서는 '숯불구이', '숯불 갈비'처럼 음식 이름 앞에 붙는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: It pairs naturally with verbs, as in '숯불에 굽다' (grill over charcoal) and '숯불을 피우다' (light charcoal). On menus it often comes before a dish name, like '숯불구이' or '숯불 갈비'.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 숱이 많아서 머리를 자주 잘라요.
examples.en: My father has thick hair, so he gets haircuts often.

examples.ko: 숱이 적어서 파마를 하면 더 풍성해 보여요.
examples.en: My hair is thin, so a perm makes it look fuller.

examples.ko: 미용실에서 숱을 좀 쳐 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the hairdresser to thin my hair out a bit.

examples.ko: 숱이 많은 머리는 말리는 데 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Thick hair takes a long time to dry.
My hair is getting thinner as I age, and I'm worried.
That actor has thick eyebrows.

explain: 보통 '머리숱'처럼 붙여 쓰고, '숱이 많다/적다'로 말해요. 미용실에서는 '숱을 치다'라고 해서 머리카락 양을 줄인다는 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is usually written as '머리숱' (amount of hair) and described as '숱이 많다/적다' (thick/thin). At a hair salon, '숱을 치다' means to thin the hair out.

examples.en: The rice smells sour.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 안 넣었더니 국에서 쉰내가 나요.
examples.en: I didn't put the soup in the fridge, and now it smells sour.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 옷에서 쉰내가 나서 바로 빨았어요.
examples.en: The sweaty clothes smelled sour, so I washed them right away.
I washed the laundry again to get rid of the sour smell.
Don't eat food that smells sour.

examples.ko: 여름에는 도시락에서 쉰내가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: In summer, a lunchbox can start to smell sour.

explain: 밥이나 국이 '쉬다'(상해서 시큼해지다)에서 나는 냄새예요. 젖은 빨래나 땀 젖은 옷에서 나는 시큼한 냄새에도 써요. '쉰내가 나다'로 가장 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the smell of food like rice or soup that has gone off ('쉬다') and turned sour. It is also used for damp laundry or sweaty clothes. The usual pattern is '쉰내가 나다'.

examples.ko: 엄마는 일도 하고 육아도 하는 슈퍼우먼이에요.
examples.en: My mom is a superwoman who works and also raises children.

examples.ko: 저는 슈퍼우먼이 아니라서 혼자 다 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm not a superwoman, so I can't do everything alone.
Everyone at the company calls her a superwoman.

examples.ko: 슈퍼우먼처럼 살려고 하지 말고 좀 쉬어요.
examples.en: Don't try to live like a superwoman; get some rest.

examples.ko: 일과 가정을 다 챙기는 슈퍼우먼은 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: A superwoman who handles both work and family has a really hard time.

examples.ko: 언니는 요리도 운동도 잘해서 슈퍼우먼 같아요.
examples.en: My older sister is good at cooking and exercise, so she seems like a superwoman.

explain: 영화 속 영웅이 아니라 일, 집안일, 육아를 다 해내는 여성을 가리킬 때 많이 써요. 칭찬일 때도 있지만 '다 잘해야 한다는 부담'을 말할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used not for a movie hero but for a woman who manages work, housework and childcare all at once. It can be praise, but it also appears when people talk about the pressure to do everything well.

examples.en: I played twenty questions with my friends.
Let's guess the answer by playing twenty questions.
I was bored in the car, so we played twenty questions.
In twenty questions, you can only answer yes or no.

examples.ko: 제가 생각한 동물이 뭔지 스무고개로 맞혀 보세요.
examples.en: Try to guess which animal I'm thinking of with twenty questions.
The kids begged to play twenty questions.

explain: 한 사람이 답을 정해 두고 다른 사람들이 질문해서 맞히는 놀이예요. 질문에는 '예/아니요'로만 대답해요. 보통 '스무고개를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: One person picks an answer and the others guess it by asking questions, which can only be answered yes or no. You normally say '스무고개를 하다' (play twenty questions).

examples.en: I stuck the wrapping paper down with Scotch tape.
Could you lend me some tape?
I mended the torn paper with tape.
The tape tore off; where is the end of it?
I bought two rolls of tape at the stationery store.
Stick some tape on the corners of the poster.

explain: 원래는 한 회사의 상품 이름에서 왔지만 지금은 투명한 접착테이프를 두루 가리켜요. 줄여서 그냥 '테이프'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It came from a company's product name but now refers to clear adhesive tape in general. People often shorten it to just '테이프'.

examples.en: I had my teeth scaled at the dentist.

examples.ko: 스케일링 받고 나면 잇몸이 좀 시려요.
examples.en: After scaling, my gums feel a bit sensitive.
My teeth feel fresh after the scaling.
I called to book a scaling appointment.
I kept my mouth wide open during the scaling.
I drink a lot of coffee, so I should get my teeth scaled.

explain: 치과에서 치석을 없애는 치료를 말해요. '스케일링을 받다'가 가장 자연스럽고, '스케일링하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the dental treatment that removes tartar. '스케일링을 받다' (get scaling done) is the most natural phrase, and '스케일링하다' is also used.

examples.en: I cut out articles I like and paste them in a scrapbook.
I made a scrapbook with my travel photos.
My daughter stuck lots of stickers in her scrapbook.
My scrapbook is full of movie tickets.

examples.ko: 스크랩북 한 권이 벌써 다 찼어요.
examples.en: One scrapbook is already full.
I decorated a scrapbook with care to give to my teacher.

explain: 기사, 사진, 티켓 같은 것을 오려 붙여 모으는 공책이에요. '스크랩하다'는 신문이나 자료를 오려 모으는 동작을 말하는 동사로, 스크랩북에 붙이기 전 단계예요.
explain_en: It is a notebook where you paste clippings, photos or tickets. The verb '스크랩하다' names the earlier step of cutting out and saving articles or materials before pasting them in.

examples.en: This book has been a steady seller for ten years.

examples.ko: 서점에 가면 스테디셀러 코너가 따로 있어요.
examples.en: The bookstore has a separate steady-seller section.
It's a steady seller, so I bought it with confidence.
That snack is a long-loved steady seller.
I read a novel that is counted as a steady seller.
Unlike bestsellers, steady sellers keep selling over time.

explain: '베스트셀러'는 한동안 가장 많이 팔리는 책이고, 스테디셀러는 오랫동안 꾸준히 팔리는 책이에요. 책뿐 아니라 과자나 화장품 같은 상품에도 써요.
explain_en: A '베스트셀러' is a book that sells the most for a period, while a steady seller keeps selling for a long time. It is used not only for books but also for products like snacks and cosmetics.

examples.en: The delivery box was full of styrofoam.
Styrofoam is thrown away separately.
The fish box is made of styrofoam, so it's light.
I got hot coffee in a styrofoam cup.
My child made a boat out of styrofoam.
Bits of styrofoam were scattered on the floor.

explain: 원래 상품 이름에서 왔지만 지금은 흰색 발포 플라스틱을 두루 부르는 말이에요. 포장 상자나 일회용 컵 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It started as a product name but now generally refers to white foam plastic. It often comes up when talking about packing boxes or disposable cups.

examples.en: The cat crept closer.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 눈치를 보며 슬금슬금 방에서 나갔어요.
examples.en: The child sneaked out of the room, watching his mom's face.
I quietly got up before class ended.
My friend quietly took my snack.
I edged away from the gathering.
The puppy backed away bit by bit.

explain: '살금살금'은 소리 안 나게 조심하는 느낌이 강하고, 슬금슬금은 남이 모르게 슬쩍 움직이는 느낌이 강해요. 눈치를 보며 몰래 피하거나 다가갈 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '살금살금' stresses moving carefully without making a sound, while 슬금슬금 stresses moving slyly so others don't notice. It fits well when someone edges away or approaches while watching people's reactions.

examples.en: The child cried sadly, looking for his mother.
I saw the main character weeping sadly in the movie.
He wept sadly as he parted from his friend.
I heard sad crying all night.

examples.ko: 슬피 울던 아이가 사탕을 받고 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child who had been crying sadly smiled when she got candy.
The puppy whines sadly as it waits for its owner.

explain: 대부분 '슬피 울다'처럼 '울다'와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '슬프게 울다'라고 하는 경우가 더 많고, 슬피는 글이나 이야기에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used almost always with '울다', as in '슬피 울다' (to cry sadly). In everyday speech people more often say '슬프게 울다', while 슬피 shows up more in writing and stories.

examples.en: I went to the hospital because of my chronic headaches.

examples.ko: 그 약은 습관성이 있어서 오래 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That medicine can be habit-forming, so you shouldn't take it for long.

examples.ko: 손톱 물어뜯기는 습관성 행동일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Nail biting can be a habitual behavior.
Habitual lateness is hard to fix.
Be careful that being late doesn't become a habit.
I gained weight because of my habit of late-night snacking.

explain: '습관성 두통'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙거나 '습관성이 있다/되다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '습관적으로 늦는다'처럼 '습관적'을 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It attaches before another noun, as in '습관성 두통', or is used as '습관성이 있다/되다'. In everyday talk people more often say '습관적으로' (habitually), as in '습관적으로 늦는다'.

examples.en: This bus has a comfortable ride.

examples.ko: 새 차는 승차감이 부드러워서 멀미가 안 나요.
examples.en: The new car rides smoothly, so I don't get carsick.

examples.ko: 승차감보다 가격이 중요해서 작은 차를 샀어요.
examples.en: Price mattered more than ride comfort, so I bought a small car.
The road is bumpy, so the ride isn't great.
How was the ride in the taxi?
I'm looking for a car with a comfortable ride.

explain: 차, 버스, 기차를 탔을 때 느끼는 편안함을 말해요. '승차감이 좋다/나쁘다/편하다'로 써요. 자동차를 소개하거나 후기를 쓸 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes how comfortable it feels to ride in a car, bus or train. You say '승차감이 좋다/나쁘다/편하다'. It often appears in car introductions and reviews.

examples.en: I checked the train schedule before leaving.
The bus timetable is posted at the stop.

examples.ko: 시각표를 보니 다음 열차는 십 분 뒤예요.
examples.en: Looking at the timetable, the next train is in ten minutes.
The schedule changes during the holidays, so check it in advance.

examples.ko: 공항에서 비행기 시각표를 사진으로 찍어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I took a photo of the flight schedule at the airport.
If you follow the timetable, you won't be late.

explain: 주로 기차, 버스, 비행기의 출발·도착 시각을 적은 표에 써요. 학교 수업 같은 일정은 보통 '시간표'라고 해요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to a table of departure and arrival times for trains, buses and flights. A school class schedule is normally called '시간표'.

examples.en: It's only a matter of time before that team wins.
Getting caught is just a matter of time.
The doctor said recovery is just a matter of time.
It's only a matter of time before the baby walks.

examples.ko: 모두 알게 되는 건 시간문제니까 지금 말하는 게 나아요.
examples.en: Everyone will find out sooner or later, so it's better to say it now.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 가격이 오르는 건 시간문제일 거예요.
examples.en: If this keeps up, a price rise is just a matter of time.

explain: '시간문제예요/시간문제다'의 꼴로 많이 쓰고, 결과가 거의 확실하니 곧 그렇게 될 거라는 느낌을 줘요. 좋은 일에도 나쁜 일에도 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '시간문제예요/시간문제다', carrying the feel that the result is nearly certain and will come soon. It works for both good and bad outcomes.

examples.en: I'm looking for a part-time job paid by the hour.
It's part-time work, so I only work in the afternoon.
This parking lot charges by the hour.
I work at a school as a part-time lecturer.
Part-time jobs are popular with students.
I work full-time, not part-time.

explain: 정해진 시간만큼만 일하거나 시간 단위로 요금을 내는 방식을 말해요. 반대로 하루 종일 일하는 건 '전일제'나 '풀타임'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to working only set hours or paying per hour. Working all day is called '전일제' or '풀타임' (full-time).

examples.ko: 하늘이 시꺼메서 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sky is pitch dark, so it looks like rain soon.

examples.ko: 불에 올려 둔 냄비가 시꺼멓게 탔어요.
examples.en: The pot left on the fire got burnt jet black.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 밖에 있었더니 얼굴이 시꺼메졌어요.
examples.en: I was outside all day and my face turned dark.
The sea at night looked pitch black and scary.
I haven't cleaned, so the window frame is black with grime.
Black smoke rose up and it startled me.

explain: '검다, 까맣다'보다 아주 짙고 어두운 느낌이에요. 그을음, 때, 연기처럼 지저분하거나 무서운 느낌일 때 잘 써요. 'ㅎ' 불규칙이라 '시꺼메요, 시꺼먼'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It feels darker and heavier than '검다' or '까맣다', and suits soot, grime or smoke, or a gloomy, scary look. It is a ㅎ-irregular verb, so it becomes '시꺼메요' and '시꺼먼'.

examples.en: It was market day, so the neighborhood was bustling and noisy.

examples.ko: 교실이 시끌시끌해서 선생님 말씀이 안 들려요.
examples.en: The classroom is so noisy that I can't hear the teacher.

examples.ko: 명절에는 온 가족이 모여 집이 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: On holidays the whole family gathers and the house gets lively and loud.
I walked through the noisy market alley.
It's right before vacation, so the school is buzzing.
The office was in an uproar because of that rumor.

explain: 여러 사람이 떠들어서 어수선하게 시끄러운 모습이에요. 보통 '시끌시끌하다'로 쓰고, 소문이나 논란으로 떠들썩할 때도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a busy, noisy scene where many people are talking at once. It is mostly used as '시끌시끌하다', and also when a rumor or controversy stirs up a fuss.

examples.en: Children are splashing in the water by the stream.

examples.ko: 할머니 집 근처 시냇가에는 맑은 물이 흘러요.
examples.en: Clear water flows along the stream near Grandma's house.
Walking along the stream makes me feel good.
In summer we spread a mat by the stream and relax.
There is a small path beside the stream.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 시냇가로 가재를 잡으러 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I went to the stream to catch crayfish.

explain: '시내'는 작은 개울이라는 뜻도 있지만 '시내에 가다'처럼 도시의 중심가를 뜻하는 말로 더 자주 써서 헷갈릴 수 있어요. 시냇가는 개울 쪽이라는 뜻이 분명하고, '냇가'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '시내' can mean a small stream, but it is more often used for a city center, as in '시내에 가다', which can be confusing. 시냇가 clearly means the side of a stream, and '냇가' is also used.

examples.ko: 어머니가 시래기를 삶아서 된장에 무쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother boiled the dried greens and seasoned them with soybean paste.
Seasoned dried greens are tasty with rice.
I made braised fish with dried radish greens.

examples.ko: 겨울에 처마 밑에 시래기가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: In winter, dried greens hang under the eaves.
If the dried greens are tough, you need to boil them longer.

examples.ko: 마트에서 삶은 시래기를 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of boiled dried greens at the mart.

explain: 말려 두었다가 겨울 내내 먹는 재료라서, 쓸 때는 불리고 삶는 과정이 필요해요. 국, 나물, 조림, 밥에 두루 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is dried and kept to eat all winter, so it needs soaking and boiling before use. It is used in soups, seasoned side dishes, braises and rice dishes.

examples.en: I boiled the dried-greens soup with soybean paste dissolved in it.
I had warm siraegi soup for breakfast.
I miss the siraegi soup Mom used to make.
Siraegi soup tastes even better on cold days.
I put rice into the siraegi soup and ate it.
I ordered a set meal with siraegi soup at the restaurant.

explain: '시래기'와 '국' 사이에 사이시옷이 있어서 [시래기꾹] 또는 [시래긷꾹]으로 발음해요. 보통 된장을 풀어 끓이는 집밥 국으로 떠올려요.
explain_en: There is a sai-siot between '시래기' and '국', so it is pronounced [시래기꾹] or [시래긷꾹]. People usually think of it as a home-style soup made with soybean paste.

examples.en: I moved into a new house and gave sirutteok to the neighbors.
We steamed sirutteok for the birthday.

examples.ko: 팥 시루떡은 따뜻할 때 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Red bean sirutteok tastes good when it's warm.
Please cut me just one piece of sirutteok.

examples.ko: 할머니가 시루떡 찌는 냄새가 집에 가득했어요.
examples.en: The house was filled with the smell of Grandma steaming sirutteok.

examples.ko: 가게를 열던 날 시루떡을 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: On the day the shop opened, we shared sirutteok.

explain: '시루'라는 찜기에 쪄서 만든 떡이라 이런 이름이 붙었어요. 이사, 개업, 고사 같은 때 나눠 먹는 떡으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a rice cake steamed in a 'siru' (steamer), which gives it its name. It often appears as the rice cake shared at moves, shop openings and ritual offerings.

examples.ko: 올림픽 시상대에서 메달을 목에 거는 선수의 눈에 눈물이 맺혔어요.
examples.en: Tears welled up in the athlete's eyes as the medal was hung around the neck on the Olympic podium.

examples.ko: 시상대 맨 위에 올라선 선수가 손을 흔들었어요.
examples.en: The athlete who stood at the top of the podium waved.

examples.ko: 시상대에 오른 세 선수가 함께 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The three athletes on the podium took a photo together.
Sadly, I didn't make it onto the podium.
The national anthem played over the podium.

examples.ko: 동생은 언젠가 시상대에 서는 게 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling dreams of standing on the podium someday.

explain: '시상대에 오르다/서다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 대회에서 입상했다는 뜻으로도 자연스럽게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It pairs as '시상대에 오르다/서다' (get onto/stand on the podium). It is also a natural way to say someone placed in a competition.

examples.ko: 아기가 시시때때로 울어서 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: The baby cries at all hours, so I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 시시때때로 전화가 와서 일에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Calls keep coming at all times, so I can't focus on work.
In the mountains the weather changes all the time.
The cat scratches at the door again and again.
These days I get hungry at all hours.
My friend checks in on me every so often.

explain: 때를 가리지 않고 자주 일어난다는 뜻이고, '수시로'와 비슷해요. 계속 일어나서 조금 귀찮거나 힘들다는 느낌으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means happening often without regard to the time, and is similar to '수시로'. It is also often used with a slight feeling of annoyance or strain because it keeps happening.

examples.en: I was invited to the new product tasting event.
The mart is holding a cheese tasting.

examples.ko: 시식회에서 먹어 보고 마음에 드는 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: I tried it at the tasting event and bought what I liked.
The shop held a tasting event to celebrate its opening.

examples.ko: 시식회에 온 사람들이 맛 평가를 적었어요.
examples.en: The people who came to the tasting wrote down their opinions of the taste.
I heard there is a bread tasting this weekend.

explain: 음식을 사람들에게 맛보게 하는 행사예요. 마트의 작은 맛보기 코너는 보통 '시식 코너'라고 하고, 시식회는 좀 더 행사 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: It is an event where people taste food. A small sampling stand in a mart is usually called a '시식 코너', while 시식회 sounds more like an organized event.

examples.en: On the holiday we go to pay our respects to my husband's elders.
I bought a gift for my parents-in-law.

examples.ko: 시어른과 같이 살면 불편한 점도 있어요.
examples.en: Living with your parents-in-law has its inconveniences too.
My in-laws came to see the baby.
My friend lives with and looks after her parents-in-law.
I called my in-laws to ask how they were.

explain: 결혼한 사람이 배우자의 부모님 같은 시댁 어른을 높여 부르는 말이에요. '시부모님'도 많이 써요. '-께, 드리다, 모시다'처럼 높임 표현과 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a respectful way for a married person to refer to the elders on the spouse's side, such as the spouse's parents. '시부모님' is also commonly used. It often appears with honorific forms like '-께', '드리다' and '모시다'.

examples.en: He answered the question without hesitation.
The child drank the water in big, satisfying gulps.
It was nice to see her laugh so openly.
I asked a favor, and he granted it without any fuss.
The singer sang the high notes freely and clearly.

examples.ko: 선생님이 어려운 문제를 시원스레 풀어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher solved the hard problem for us smoothly.

explain: 망설이거나 막힘 없이 거침없이 하는 태도나 모습을 말해요. 날씨나 온도가 시원하다는 뜻이 아니라 사람의 행동과 모습에 주로 써요. '시원하게'와 비슷하지만 사람의 태도를 말할 때 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes doing something without hesitation or hitch, in a free and unhindered way. It is not about cool temperatures; it is mainly used for a person's actions and manner. It is close to '시원하게' but fits better when describing someone's attitude.
